answer: Bonded identity resists sybils: a new agent must lock a stake in a shared vault before earning, and the bond stays non-transferable until many epochs of peer-attested work pass. An attacker wanting a thousand identities must fund a thousand deposits locked for months. Rewards vest slowly, and one failed attestation slashes the bond, so each fake account becomes a forfeitable loss, not a throwaway. The registry can harbor no anonymous entries, since blind grading blocks self-vouching clusters. A prism splits light; this rule splits one reputation into obligations backed by separate collateral.
